prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Checkout UI Strings (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Key" · longest unbreakable word 206px · one-line width 206px
  col 2: header "English" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 196px
  col 3: header "中文" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 184px
  col 4: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 283px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 187px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare checkout interface strings across four languages, using stable keys to identify each message.","reading":"Readers scan the key column to find a message, then read across its row to compare translations. Each row should remain a clear unit even when translations wrap.","groups":["English, 中文, 日本語, and العربية are parallel translations of the same message and should have a comparable visual role.","Key is the row identifier and needs enough width for the longest unbroken identifier."],"keep_intact":["Keys and other unbreakable words","Numeric ranges such as 3–5"],"may_wrap":["Translation phrases at natural word or character boundaries","Shorter translations can remain on one line while longer translations use the row height created by another language."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [225, 124, 109, 143, 116] · table 718×371px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 83, 36, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [225, 148, 99, 131, 114] · table 718×371px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 83, 36, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [225, 111, 94, 158, 129] · table 718×418px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 83, 36, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Constraint adjustments applied: r0A: scaled down from 724px to fit 719px
r0B: scaled down from 724px to fit 719px
r0C: scaled down from 724px to fit 719px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
